newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Market sideways in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Market sideways in quiet trade.

text.p: Singapore oil product swaps were drifting sideways in quiet trade in the absence of fresh physical indicators, traders said.
"The market is drifting as there is not much going on," one trader said.
Fuel oil swaps were last quoted firmer at $97.00/$98.00 per barrel for May and June, up from Monday's $96.50/$97.50, brokers said.
The May/June spread traded earlier in the day at flat, they said.
Traders said the market is looking to fresh physical trading to spur the market. On Tuesday, a bid for a 20,000-tonne cargo was heard at $97.00 per tonne but no sellers emerged against it.
"The bid was relatively low. it is not doing anything to the market," a trader said.

Gas oil was quoted unchanged in lacklustre trading with prices continuing to get support from a buying spree by the Singapore traders who bought another 300,000 barrels of physical cargoes on Tuesday, bringing their total to nearly 14 million barrels.
May gas oil swaps was quoted steady from Tuesday at $25.55/$25.70 per barrel, while June was indicated at $24.30/$24.60, down 20 cents.
Brokers said June traded in the morning at $24.60 and $24.65 per barrel.
The jet fuel/gas oil spread or regrade has widened with May seen at minus 60/45 cents a barrel, compared with Tuesday's minus 45/25 cents.
May regrade traded earlier in the day at minus 50 cents, they said.
